Unrounded vowels come before the dot, rounded after it. Length: long vowels aː. Nasality: no nasal vowels. Phonation: i‼ u‼ ɜ̠‼.

### Tone, syllables and stress

| tone | IPA | spelling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| low | a˨ | grave à |

| high | a˦ | acute á |
| rising | a˨˦ | caron ǎ |

The language has 5 phonemic tones, marked on every vowel in the IPA here.
Syllable shapes (share of syllables in the word-shape model): CV 33%, CVC 29%, CCV 13%, CCVC 10%, CVCC 6%, V 4%, VC 3%, CCVCC 2%. At most 2 consonant(s) before the vowel and 2 after it.
Stress falls on the next-to-last syllable.
Core words average 1.97 syllables (3.5 sounds); 11% of words share their form with another word.

### Allophony

This output records no allophones (the engine stores sounds as phonemes only).

## Orthography

The house romanization in two registers: the full spelling (workbench, one letter or digraph per sound, tone marks) and the book spelling (lossy: no tone, plain vowels, at most one diacritic letter a word).

**Consonants:** m ‹m› · n ‹n› · ŋ ‹ng› · p ‹p› · t̪ ‹t̪› ‹t› · d̪ ‹d̪› ‹d› · t ‹t› · k ‹k› · ʔ ‹'› · tʃ ‹ch› · s ‹s› · ʂ ‹ṣ› · v ‹v› · ʁ ‹ġ› · ħ ‹ḥ› · ʕ ‹ʿ› · h ‹h› · ɦ ‹hh› · ɬ ‹hl› · ɮ ‹dl› · ɹ ‹ř› ‹r› · ɻ ‹ḻ› · j ‹y› · w ‹w› · j‼ ‹yrh› · l ‹l› · ɾ‼ ‹rrh›

**Vowels:** i ‹i› · i‼ ‹irh› · y ‹ü› · ɨ̠ ‹ï̠› ‹ï› · u‼ ‹urh› · e ‹e› · ɛ ‹è› ‹e› · ɜ̠‼ ‹erh› · ʌ̞ ‹e̞o› ‹eo› · a ‹a› · aː ‹aa›

Tones are written over the vowel: low grave à, mid unmarked a, high acute á, rising caron ǎ, falling circumflex â (Yoruba-style).

Where two spellings are given the second is the book spelling.

## Grammar

Basic word order is SOV; it has postpositions. In the noun phrase: possessor before the possessed; adjective before the noun; demonstrative before the noun; noun before the numeral; relative clause before the noun. Overall it is head-final.
It has a definite article before the noun, an indefinite article, a few cases, nominative-accusative alignment, singular and plural, a system of noun classes.
Verbs mark past, future, perfective and progressive; there are no evidentials. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use a final question particle. Verbs agree with the subject by prefixes; not with the object.
Other features: serial verbs; verb reduplication; adjectives that behave like verbs; a bound causative; no passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base; a 'have' verb for possession.
Measured morphology: 22 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 1.4 (0 free word … 3 fused), 64 paradigm cells, 4 of them with allomorphy.
